title: Bring It On
about: A new cheer captain finds out her squad's winning routines were stolen from a Compton team, and has to build her own before nationals.
cue: Bring out the churros when Torrance drops the Spirit Stick at cheer camp.

    SnacksSparky's spirit fingersSparky Polastri's famous spirit fingers. Crumbed chicken tenders, honey mustard dip.How to make it600g chicken tenderloins75g plain flour2 eggs120g panko breadcrumbs40g parmesan, finely grated1 tsp smoked paprika3 tbsp olive oil3 tbsp Dijon mustard3 tbsp honey3 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaiseSeason the flour, beat the eggs, and mix the panko with the parmesan and paprika.Dip each tender in flour, egg, then crumbs, and lay on a lined tray.Drizzle with oil and bake at 220°C, turning once, until golden and cooked through.Stir the mustard, honey and mayo together and serve with the tenders.Car wash fish tacosThe Toros' car wash fundraiser. San Diego fish tacos, cabbage, chipotle crema.How to make it500g firm white fish fillets, cut in strips100g plain flour150ml chilled soda water1 tsp ground cumin500ml vegetable oil, for frying8 small corn tortillas1/4 white cabbage, finely shredded125g sour cream1 tbsp chipotle in adobo, chopped2 limes1/2 cup coriander leavesStir the sour cream with the chipotle and a squeeze of lime.Whisk the flour, cumin, a pinch of salt and the soda water into a light batter.Dip the fish and fry in hot oil in batches until crisp and golden.Warm the tortillas in a dry pan.Fill with cabbage and fish, spoon over the crema and finish with coriander and lime.I'm sexy, I'm cute popcornPopular to boot. Red and white, for the Toros.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.GrillRancho Carne carne asada platesHome of the Rancho Carne Toros. Grilled skirt steak, pico de gallo, rice and beans.How to make it800g skirt steak3 limes1 orange3 garlic cloves, crushed1 tsp ground cumin2 tbsp olive oil300g long-grain rice400g tin black beans, drained3 tomatoes, diced1/2 white onion, finely diced1 cup coriander, chopped8 small flour tortillasMarinate the steak in the juice of 2 limes and the orange, the garlic, cumin, oil and salt for at least 20 minutes.Cook the rice, then stir through the warmed beans and a squeeze of lime.Mix the tomato, onion, coriander and remaining lime juice into a pico de gallo.Grill the steak over high heat, 3 minutes a side, rest it, then slice thinly across the grain.Serve with the rice and beans, pico and warm tortillas.Daytona Cuban sandwichesDaytona, where the Clovers win. Roast pork, ham, Swiss, pickles, pressed hot.How to make it4 long crusty rolls300g roast pork, thinly sliced200g shaved leg ham8 slices of Swiss cheese1 cup dill pickle slices4 tbsp yellow mustard40g soft butterSplit the rolls and spread both sides with mustard.Layer the pork, ham, cheese and pickles, then close.Butter the outsides and press in a hot pan under a heavy pan, turning once, until crisp and melted.Cut on the diagonal and serve hot.SweetsSpirit Stick churrosThe Spirit Stick never touches the ground. Cinnamon sugar churros, thick chocolate.How to make it250ml water60g butter1 tbsp caster sugar, plus 100g for rolling150g plain flour2 eggs2 tsp ground cinnamon1 L vegetable oil, for frying150g dark chocolate, chopped200ml thickened creamBring the water, butter, 1 tbsp sugar and a pinch of salt to the boil, tip in the flour and beat until it leaves the pan.Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time until glossy.Heat the cream, pour over the chocolate and stir until smooth.Pipe 12cm lengths into oil at 180°C and fry in batches until golden.Roll in the remaining sugar mixed with the cinnamon and serve with the dip.DrinksCliff's minty lime coolerBrushing teeth with Cliff, not a word said. Lime, crushed mint and soda over ice.How to make it1 cup mint leaves100g caster sugar100ml water4 limes750ml soda water2 cups ice cubesHeat the sugar and water until dissolved, add half the mint and cool.Muddle the remaining mint with lime juice in 4 glasses.Add the strained syrup and ice and top with soda.Clovers lime sodaEast Compton's finest.
